title: Tadalafil
description: How tadalafil relaxes blood vessels, its established uses and the mixed findings in Raynaud studies.
scope: Tadalafil in erectile dysfunction, benign prostatic hyperplasia, pulmonary arterial hypertension and secondary Raynaud phenomenon.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Tadalafil inhibits PDE5, an enzyme involved in smooth-muscle relaxation. It is used for erectile dysfunction, urinary symptoms from benign prostatic hyperplasia and, under a separate indication, pulmonary arterial hypertension. Cialis and Adcirca contain the same active ingredient but cover different labeled uses and regimens. The pulmonary indication is specifically WHO group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension, so it does not include every type of pulmonary hypertension. Repurposing research has also examined secondary Raynaud phenomenon, where reduced finger circulation produces a separate vascular question. Two small crossover studies reached conflicting symptom findings. One tested an add-on to existing vasodilators and observed fewer attacks and improved ulcer healing; the other did not show a symptom advantage over placebo. Thus the vascular rationale and established indications provide context, while Raynaud benefit remains a separate clinical question.

sections.label: Benefits
sections.paragraph: Pulmonary arterial hypertension is an established tadalafil indication. Research in secondary Raynaud phenomenon is mixed: one small add-on trial reported improved attacks and ulcer healing, while another found no symptom advantage over placebo. The positive 2010 study tested tadalafil alongside existing vasodilators and reported fewer and shorter Raynaud attacks. All 24 existing digital lesions healed during tadalafil treatment compared with three of thirteen during placebo, but these are lesion counts rather than patient response rates. New ulcers numbered one during tadalafil and thirteen during placebo. The 2009 trial found no difference in attacks or condition score. Its negative result should remain visible beside the positive add-on findings. These small crossover comparisons differed in populations and treatment schedules, leaving uncertainty about which patients benefit and under what background treatment rather than establishing a uniform Raynaud effect.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Tadalafil commonly causes headache, flushing, indigestion, back pain or muscle discomfort, but its important hazards include excessive blood-pressure lowering with particular co-medications. Nitrates and riociguat are contraindicated, while alpha blockers, other antihypertensives and substantial alcohol exposure have separate hypotension precautions. The labels also discuss prolonged erection and sudden visual or hearing changes as issues distinct from routine transient adverse effects. Kidney and liver impairment can affect the dosing or suitability assessment, with different qualifications for the erectile-dysfunction/BPH and pulmonary-hypertension products. These distinctions matter when interpreting Raynaud studies that add tadalafil to an existing vasodilator regimen. A small trial cannot define the frequency of uncommon serious events or clear every cardiovascular combination. The actual product, dose schedule, background therapy and clinical population must remain attached to any statement about tolerability or benefit.

sections.label: Contraindications
sections.paragraph: The tadalafil labels contraindicate concomitant organic nitrates because tadalafil can potentiate their blood-pressure-lowering effect. They also prohibit concomitant soluble guanylate-cyclase stimulators such as riociguat and use after serious hypersensitivity to tadalafil. These restrictions are different from the precautions applied to alpha blockers, other antihypertensive medicines, alcohol exposure and certain cardiovascular conditions. The actual product and indication also matter: erectile-dysfunction/BPH and pulmonary-hypertension labeling have their own dose and population qualifications. A general statement that tadalafil improves blood flow therefore cannot establish that adding it to another vasodilator is safe. When it is investigated for Raynaud phenomenon or another repurposed use, the study's screening criteria do not replace the formal contraindications. The full medication context, kidney and liver function and the actual dosing schedule remain necessary to interpret those restrictions.

sections.label: Interactions
sections.paragraph: Tadalafil interactions can arise from additive vasodilation or changes in metabolic clearance. Nitrates and riociguat have explicit contraindications, whereas alpha blockers and other antihypertensive agents have their own blood-pressure precautions. Substantial alcohol intake can also increase orthostatic symptoms because alcohol and tadalafil both have vasodilating effects. Potent CYP3A inhibitors can increase tadalafil exposure, and enzyme inducers can lower it, with product-specific dosing or use qualifications. These mechanisms should remain separate rather than being summarized as one general cardiovascular interaction. The longer persistence of tadalafil also matters to the label's discussion of nitrate exposure after a dose. A Raynaud trial involving selected background vasodilators does not establish compatibility with every additional blood-pressure medicine or metabolic inhibitor. The actual product, schedule, interacting agent and population must be preserved when interpreting a repurposing combination.

sections.label: Dosing
sections.paragraph: The Raynaud trials tested 20 mg daily for four weeks or 20 mg on alternate days for six weeks; neither establishes a universal Raynaud regimen. The labeled adult pulmonary-hypertension regimen is 40 mg once daily, with kidney, liver and interaction restrictions. The daily four-week Raynaud schedule and the alternate-day six-week schedule are distinct protocols, with different populations and background treatment. The positive add-on study therefore cannot be assumed to validate the negative trial's daily regimen, or vice versa. Adcirca's labeled 40 mg daily schedule addresses WHO group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension, a different indication from secondary Raynaud phenomenon. Cialis and Adcirca also have different labeled uses and regimens despite sharing tadalafil as their active ingredient. Dose interpretation must therefore retain the product, indication, duration and treatment context rather than selecting a milligram amount from one study as a general vascular schedule.

sections.label: Results
sections.paragraph: The negative Raynaud crossover trial had 39 evaluable participants. In the positive trial, 24 of 25 recruited participants completed follow-up; new digital ulcers numbered one during tadalafil and 13 during placebo.

sections.label: Quality
sections.paragraph: The tadalafil products cited here share an active molecule but have different labeled indications and dosing schedules. The erectile-dysfunction and benign-prostatic-hyperplasia product has its own daily or as-needed administration instructions, while the pulmonary-arterial-hypertension product is evaluated in a different disease and treatment setting. A product name or milligram amount alone therefore does not identify the complete tested intervention. Strength, administered frequency, indication, kidney and liver qualifications and accompanying medicines also matter. Those distinctions remain relevant to Raynaud research, where studies can use their own schedules and background vasodilators. Neither an established pulmonary-hypertension indication nor equivalence of the active molecule proves benefit for that separate condition. Product labeling supplies formulation, administration and restriction information, while the actual Raynaud trial supplies the clinical comparison. Results should not be transferred between regimens merely because all of them contain tadalafil.

sections.label: Status
sections.paragraph: US labeling covers erectile dysfunction and benign prostatic hyperplasia for Cialis, and WHO group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension for Adcirca. Raynaud phenomenon is outside these labeled indications.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: Both Raynaud trials used crossover designs and small samples. Their conflicting results leave uncertainty about which patients benefit from tadalafil and under which background treatment. The negative 2009 study had 39 evaluable participants. In the positive 2010 add-on study, 24 of 25 recruited participants completed follow-up, and improvements concerned attacks and digital lesions during treatment alongside existing vasodilators. Counts of healed lesions do not represent separate patients and should not be converted into a patient response proportion. The studies also used different dosing schedules and treatment durations, making the disagreement clinically relevant rather than a duplicate estimate from an identical intervention. Together they support uncertainty about the appropriate Raynaud population and background therapy. Neither comparison expands the labeled pulmonary indication beyond WHO group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension.

faqs.question: Is every type of pulmonary hypertension a tadalafil indication?
faqs.answer: No. The Adcirca indication specifies pulmonary arterial hypertension in WHO group 1.

faqs.question: Why are nitrates a major interaction?
faqs.answer: Combining nitrates with tadalafil can produce a dangerous fall in blood pressure. The label specifies at least 48 hours after the last tadalafil dose before nitrate consideration in a life-threatening emergency, with close medical monitoring.
